arm_comparison.causality: No causal exclusion claim: core service code for both full-only supported manifestations remained identical in candidate. One stochastic call per arm cannot separate attention/context effects from sampling variation.
arm_comparison.cost_quality_interpretation: Observed input reduction is5.8779 percent. Candidate did not surface every supported manifestation raised by full, so no quality-parity claim. This four-PR comparison is not defect recall and does not establish downstream savings at equal quality.
arm_comparison.grouping_caveat: Forward/reverse admission-dispatch confusion share a missing type/lifecycle boundary; concurrent report replay is a distinct path. These lists are manifestations, not a calibrated defect count or recall denominator.

other_prs.357: Neither V2 arm reported a finding. Prior Import staging concern remains a separate partial-support adjudication, not a newly detected V2 finding.

arm_comparison.unchanged_dependency_context: CompleteClaim and Claim implementations are absent as declaration bodies from both packets; adjudication inspected them independently at the pinned revision.

findings.impact_bound: False successful acknowledgement of a differing report; durable record remains B outcome, not a demonstrated second write or outcome overwrite. Same principal, valid authorization, claim identity and expected version still required.
interleaving: Reports A and B use the same admission token and different valid outcomes.
A reads version v, state claimed through Report.authorizedCurrent; A pauses before calling CompleteClaim.
B completes and commits its different outcome at version v+1 under the same claim.
A enters CompleteClaim, which reads the now-terminal record and returns it with nil error from its terminal replay branch.
Report A accepts that nil error and reports success without checking whether the returned outcome matches A.
findings.proof_limit: No concurrency reproduction executed; pinned control flow supports the explicit interleaving.
findings.recommendation: Validate returned successful completion against sameReportedOutcome and normalized output, or implement an outcome-aware completion primitive that enforces admission replay semantics for every interleaving.
findings.why_cas_does_not_prevent: In this interleaving A never attempts a mutation or CAS. It takes CompleteClaim terminal replay after B has already committed. Other timings may conflict; the claim need not occur on every concurrent call.
findings.witness: Report checks current.State.terminal() on its first read, but after CompleteClaim returns nil error it returns that record without sameReportedOutcome validation. CompleteClaim re-reads current and terminal-replays solely on state/version/claim, without comparing output or failure code.

confirmed_manifestations.witness: The grant exposes action ID, TokenID=ClaimID and version. Generic HTTP complete forwards these to bound CompleteClaim, then DispatchService.CompleteClaim. No layer excludes records with nonempty AdmittedEffects. A later differing completion under the same expected version and claim succeeds through terminal replay without outcome equality, unlike AdmissionService.Report intended contract.

confirmed_manifestations.bound: Original admission obligations are not recomputed by Claim. Claim still reauthorizes principal and current descriptor; authorized effect ceiling remains in force. No unpermitted external effect was dynamically demonstrated.
confirmed_manifestations.witness: Claim rejects live claimed records and terminal states, but accepts an expired DispatchClaimed admission before its action deadline. It clones the record, increments version/fence, installs a new claim ID/lease, and resolves ordinary descriptor effects. AdmittedEffects validation enforces declaration shape only; it does not forbid claimed-to-claimed transitions. Pull also includes expired claimed admissions.

findings.proof_limit: Static code and handler inspection; no HTTP exploit or external-effect reproduction.
findings.recommendation: Separate admissions from dispatch records/routes or explicitly reject admission records in generic Pull/Claim/Complete/Execute paths, with a shared internal completion primitive reserved for legitimate Report calls.
refuted_or_unproven_extensions: Canceled/denied admissions cannot be reclaimed: Claim checks current.State.terminal() and returns ErrActionTerminal.
No cross-principal takeover: authorizedCurrent verifies subject, actor, client, delegation chain, object and registry binding.
No claim of execution beyond registry/executor effect ceilings; the narrower admission lifecycle is bypassed, while ordinary dispatch authorization remains enforced.

findings.candidate_difference: Candidate did not report this direction of type confusion. Outstanding, Report and admitted full source are byte-identical and retained in both packets; no causal evidence that code omission caused the difference.
findings.impact_bound: An invoke-only client with the same subject/actor/client/delegation tuple can newly learn a live worker claim and submit completion through admission. No cross-principal access established.
findings.relationship: Shares missing admission-versus-dispatch discrimination with reverse-direction finding; do not count the two directions as wholly independent root causes without an explicit counting rule.
findings.witness: Outstanding includes ordinary live dispatch claims because it filters state/principal but not AdmittedEffects. It returns ClaimID as TokenID. Report forwards that token to CompleteClaim without admission discrimination. Pre-existing invoke Pull withholds unexpired claimed records; Status requires dispatch permission.
Store cursor is raw action ID. Outstanding returns it before principal filtering. Existing invoke Pull already exposes the identical cursor behavior.

Valid authorized request yields conflict for an occupied guessed ID and proceeds for an unused one. Existing enqueue/Invoke already behaves this way. queuedRecord authorizes the supplied target before lookup; equivalentEnqueue binds principal and authorization fingerprint.
